statement: A byte string whose nesting depth exceeds gx's ceiling (64 levels) is not decoded
deviation: Nested `[ {"a": ...} ]` 33 times, placing the integer 0 at the innermost point. The scanner's depth increases by 1 for an array element and by 1 each for a map's key and value, so one nesting = 2 levels. The 33rd map header reaches depth 65, becoming TooDeep at `depth > MAX_DEPTH` (64). **It violates no clause of 42 §2.1 at all** -- this byte string is fully canonical as IPLD DAG-CBOR. The basis for refusing it is 41 §6's panic=bug lineage: the recursive scanner is protected from having its stack exhausted by hostile input, by a ceiling rather than by a type (`cbor.rs`'s `MAX_DEPTH` doc, verbatim: "shallow enough that a hostile input cannot exhaust the stack before scan_strict returns"). Hence `normative_basis` is gx-policy, neither IPLD-MUST nor IPLD-SHOULD.
spec_anchor: 41 §6(panic=bug) / 42 §2.1(explicitly stating this clause does not apply) / req/38 §17 F-2
origin: gx self-authored for hand 7 (req/38 §17 F-2's ruling)

control.note: The same shape, 32 times -- the innermost point is exactly depth 64. The ceiling is "refuse past 64", not "refuse at 64", so this is accepted. Moving the ceiling comparison from `>` to `>=` **drops this control** -- the negative vector alone cannot tell anyone which side of the boundary the line is drawn on
